cases.title: Ice arrows
cases.semanticExcerpt:
'''Ice arrows''' are a [[quest item]] in the [[Temple of Ikov]] [[quest]]. They have the same [[Ranged Strength]] as [[steel arrow]]s, but must be fired from a [[yew bow]] or better.

In the Temple of Ikov quest, they are collected randomly when searching [[Closed chest (Temple of Ikov)|chests]] in the eastern [[Temple of Ikov (dungeon)|Temple of Ikov dungeon]] and required to defeat the [[Fire Warrior of Lesarkus]]. While not required, ice arrows can also be used to defeat [[Fareed]] from the [[Desert Treasure I]] quest, as all other ammunition will drop to the floor as [[ashes]], bypassing the ammo-saving effect of [[Ava's device]]s.

Upon completion of the quest, players can still go back and obtain more should they desire it.

cases.title: Dark dagger
cases.semanticExcerpt:
'''dark dagger''' is a [[quest item]] obtained during [[Legends' Quest]]. It is given to the player by the entity [[Echned Zekin]]. The dagger can then either be given to [[Ugandulu]] for a one-use [[Holy force]] spell, or used to kill [[Viyeldi]] which converts the dagger into a [[glowing dagger]]. It is then given to Echned, who turns out to be the [[Nezikchened|demon]].

If players have misplaced their glowing dagger after the quest, it can be reclaimed from [[Radimus Erkle]], and can be investigated via-right click afterwards to switch its appearance between a dark or glowing dagger.

It has the same stats as an [[iron dagger]] albeit without a [[strength bonus]].

cases.title: Glowing dagger
cases.semanticExcerpt:
'''glowing dagger''' is a [[quest items|quest item]] obtained and used during the [[Legends' Quest]]. It has the same combat stats as an [[iron dagger]], only lacking the +4 strength bonus.

It is created when players are given the [[dark dagger]] by [[Echned Zekin]], requesting them to kill [[Viyeldi]] because he was the one that murdered him and wants revenge. Once the dagger is used to kill Viyeldi, it will convert into a glowing dagger. It can then be taken back to Echned Zekin, who will reveal his true form - the demon [[Nezikchened]]. Alternatively, it can be taken to [[Ungadulu]].

Players can obtain another glowing dagger after the quest by speaking to [[Radimus Erkle]] in the [[Legends' Guild]], and can be investigated via-right click afterwards to switch its appearance between a dark or glowing dagger.

cases.title: Phoenix crossbow
cases.semanticExcerpt:
'''Phoenix crossbow''' is a [[quest item]], although it can be traded. It has the same stats as a regular [[crossbow]] except for attack range, but weighs significantly less. It can be obtained and is used in the quest [[Shield of Arrav]]. The Phoenix crossbow has no requirements to wield, and can only fire [[bronze bolts]]. It can also be used with a [[mith grapple]] for Agility shortcuts.

The Phoenix crossbow is not often used, as the [[bronze crossbow]] requires the same [[Ranged]] level to equip, but gives a Ranged accuracy of +18, whilst the Phoenix crossbow only gives +6. However, the Phoenix crossbow is essentially free, and since bronze crossbows and above are [[members-only]] items, the Phoenix crossbow is the second-best crossbow available to [[free-to-play]] players. While the Phoenix crossbow is lighter than and has the same +6 range bonus as the standard [[crossbow]], the Phoenix crossbow has a maximum range of 7 tiles, whereas the standard crossbow has a range of 10 tiles.

cases.title: Chaos gauntlets
cases.semanticExcerpt:
'''Before Family Pest:''' You can obtain another set of chaos gauntlets from Dimintheis.
'''After Family Pest:''' You can obtain another set of chaos gauntlets from Johnathon. |examine = These gauntlets empower spell casters. |value = 1 |weight = 0.226 |id = 777 }} [[File:Chaos gauntlets detail.png|left|130px]] '''Chaos gauntlets''' are a pair of [[gloves]] available after completing the quest [[Family Crest]], along with the [[goldsmith gauntlets|goldsmith]] and [[cooking gauntlets]]. The gauntlets, when worn, increase the maximum damage done by all [[bolt spells]] by 3 (before the boosted damage is multiplied by [[Magic damage|Magic Damage]] stats), thus making the max hit of bolt spells only 1 below that of [[blast spells]] and [[Inferior Demonbane]]. There are no requirements to wear these gloves. Players can obtain the chaos gauntlets by bringing the [[steel gauntlets]] that were awarded from the quest to [[Johnathon]], located upstairs in the [[Jolly Boar Inn]], which is north-east of [[Varrock]]. (Note: if the gauntlets have a different enchantment on them already, Johnathon will charge the player 25,000 [[coins]]). The text that appears when you give your gauntlets to Johnathon is: "''Johnathon takes your gauntlets from you, and begins a low chant over them. You see them glow and sparkle, before he returns them to you.''" Prior to completing the [[Family Pest]] [[miniquest]], if lost, they are re-obtained free of charge from [[Dimintheis]]. After completion of the Family Pest, they can be claimed from Johnathon for free at any time and without the need for steel gauntlets; and all forms of the Family Crest gauntlets can be owned simultaneously. They can also be claimed in [[free-to-play]] [[Server|worlds]] but cannot be equipped in free-to-play. Upon death, they will be lost unless they are a protected item.

Before completion of the [[Family Pest]] [[miniquest]], players can only have one pair of gauntlets at a time. After completing the miniquest, [[Dimintheis]] will hand the player as many pairs of steel gauntlets as they want for free.

cases.title: Oak longbow
cases.semanticExcerpt:
'''oak longbow''' is a [[longbow (weapon)|longbow]] made from oak. It can be made at level 25 [[Fletching]] by using a [[knife]] on [[oak logs]] to cut them into an [[oak longbow (u)]], granting 25 experience, and then using a [[bowstring]] on the unstrung bow, granting another 25 experience. It requires level 5 [[Ranged]] to wield and can fire arrows up to and including [[steel arrow|steel]].

It has identical stats to the [[oak shortbow]], but fires at a slower [[attack speed|speed]].

During the quest [[Ghosts Ahoy]] a player might acquire a [[signed oak bow]] which is exactly the same as the oak longbow, aside from its name.

Fletching an oak longbow from [[oak logs]] and a [[bow string]] will profit {{Coins|{{GEP|Oak longbow}}-({{GEP|Oak logs}}+{{GEP|Bow string}})}} while fletching an oak longbow from an [[oak longbow (u)]] and a [[bow string]] will profit {{Coins|{{GEP|Oak longbow}}-({{GEP|Oak longbow (u)}}+{{GEP|Bow string}})}}.

cases.title: Yew longbow
cases.semanticExcerpt:
'''yew longbow''' is a [[longbow (weapon)|longbow]] stronger than the [[maple longbow]] that can use arrows up to [[rune arrow|rune]]. The yew longbow requires a [[Ranged]] level of 40 or higher to wield.

Players can make a yew longbow through the [[Fletching]] skill at level 70. First, a player must cut a [[yew longbow (u)]] from [[yew logs]], giving 75 Fletching [[experience]]. The unstrung bow is then strung with a [[bow string]], for an additional 75 experience for a total of 150 experience a log. It can also be obtained as a very rare drop from a [[young impling]].

Fletching a yew longbow from [[yew logs]] and a [[bow string]] will profit {{Coins|{{GEP|Yew longbow}}-({{GEP|Yew logs}}+{{GEP|Bow string}})}} while fletching a yew longbow from a [[yew longbow (u)]] and a [[bow string]] will profit {{Coins|{{GEP|Yew longbow}}-({{GEP|Yew longbow (u)}}+{{GEP|Bow string}})}}.

Creating a yew longbow from scratch in [[Seers' Village]] is a task for the [[Kandarin Diary#Hard|Kandarin hard diary]].

cases.title: Zamorak monk top
cases.semanticExcerpt:
'''Zamorak monk top''' is part of the [[Zamorak monk robes]] set. They are bright red, and like the related [[Zamorak monk bottom]] they are dropped by [[Disciple of Iban|disciples of Iban]], necromancers and [[monks of Zamorak]].

Zamorak monk robes are commonly used by mages in the [[Wilderness]] due to providing decent [[Prayer]] and [[Magic]] bonuses and being easy to replace if lost. They can also be used to telegrab [[Wine of Zamorak]] at the [[Chaos Temple (Asgarnia)]] without being attacked.

One of only three [[Body slot table (F2P)|free-to-play bodies]] with a magic attack bonus, the Zamorak monk top has 1 less [[Magic]] attack and 3 more [[Prayer]] bonus when compared to the [[Black robe]], [[Blue wizard robe]], and their [[Ornamental armour|ornamental variants]]. 

The Zamorak monk top counts as a [[Zamorak item]] in the [[God Wars Dungeon]].
